facts.fact: Egypt's answers to the WHO EMRO CRVS questionnaire state that paper notifications are collected from health offices, sent to the local Civil Registry Office, then to the governorate's Civil Registry offices and then to the governorate Civil Status Information Center, where they are processed electronically and compiled centrally; the document gives no date for this, so its published year is used.
facts.system: Civil Status civil registration system (governorate Civil Status Information Center)

facts.fact: The questionnaire states that birth and death notifications alike pass on paper to the governorate Civil Status Information Center, where they are entered electronically, and that birth and death records are archived electronically; no date is given, so the published year is used.
facts.system: Civil Status civil registration system (governorate Civil Status Information Center)

facts.fact: Asked what equipment all or most civil registration points have, Egypt answered no to telephones, photocopiers, scanners, computers and internet, and wrote 'Paper' under other; no date is given, so the published year is used.

The questionnaire states that local registration offices record and store births and deaths in registry books in all provinces and in electronic files 'approximately in some provinces', with no count of offices or provinces; it gives the number of local civil registrars as 378 or 878 (the extraction shows both); no date is given, so the published year is used.

Egypt reports that in the last decade a pilot project was developed to perform electronic registration of births and deaths at Health Office level in some selected governorates, that work is currently electronic at health directorate level and that an automation project is under implementation in health offices; no date or number of offices is given, so the published year is used.
facts.system: Pilot electronic registration at Health Office level

facts.fact: The questionnaire names the Civil Status Authority and its governorate Civil Status Information Centers as the bodies that enter and hold the civil record electronically, with the Ministry of Health running the health offices that take the notifications; no date is given, so the published year is used.
facts.system: Civil Status civil registration system (governorate Civil Status Information Center)

facts.fact: Egypt gave no figure for the annual national operating budget for civil registration, answered that it cannot be separately identified at national, state or municipal level and that the funds are not adequate, and said extra funding would matter most in the Ministry of Health and Civil Status Authority offices; no date is given, so the published year is used.
facts.system: Civil Status civil registration system (governorate Civil Status Information Center)

systems.tiers: named in a question on coding; no answer extracted

note: The document is undated internally; its latest cited data year is 2011 and its published date in the list is 2025-01-01, which is used as as_of throughout. It answers 'No' to mobile registration facilities in remote areas. Whether the health office is the registration point or only notifies is stated both ways in the document: it calls health offices civil registration offices and also says they take notifications that the Civil Registry compiles.
